articleBody:
Before you sign a contract or swing a hammer on a kitchen bump-out, make sure you have every detail documented to keep the project on track and avoid unexpected delays. 

- [ ] Property boundary survey — Confirms your exterior addition complies with local zoning setbacks and easements.
- [ ] Measured floor plan drawings — Verifies exact cabinet dimensions, aisle clearances, and appliance placement before ordering materials.
- [ ] Electrical panel service capacity check — Ensures your current service panel can supply added circuits for high-draw kitchen appliances.
- [ ] Written building permit responsibilities — Spells out clearly whether the general contractor applies for, pulls, and manages all municipal permits.
- [ ] Itemized material allowance breakdown — Gives transparent budgets for cabinetry, tile, marble, countertops, and finish fixtures.
- [ ] Schedule of required trade inspections — Outlines when rough framing, plumbing, electrical, and insulation checks must occur before drywall.
- [ ] Written change-order procedure — Clarifies how scope adjustments, hidden framing issues, and cost modifications are approved in writing.
- [ ] Clean-up and debris disposal agreement — Details on-site dumpster placement and daily broom-clean expectations during structural work.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through each line item with your builder before signing an agreement. Having these specific documents and expectations confirmed upfront prevents unexpected budget overruns and ensures framing and trade rough-ins move forward without code delays.
